title: Ancient DNA: what the studies on this map measure
fact_summary: Ancient DNA studies read genetic material from skeletons. The studies on this map report three kinds of result, and each answers a different question.

claims.text: The studies report maternal lineages (mitochondrial DNA), paternal lineages (Y chromosome), and genome-wide or “shotgun” genome data.
claims.certainty_reason: All three study types are named in the abstracts read.

claims.text: Ancestry is reported by modelling a group as a mix of reference populations, for example “50% Mansi, 35% Early/Late Sarmatian”, and the time of mixing is estimated in generations before death.
claims.certainty_reason: This records what the study reports, read in the open copy linked under Sources.

claims.text: Samples are often chosen from rich graves. One study sampled individuals “supposed to represent the power/military elit[e]”; another included the 8 richest Avar-period burials.
claims.certainty_reason: This records what the study reports, read in the open copy linked under Sources.

claims.text: Results can differ sharply between elite groups and everyone else: one study reports that most individuals in each period were local, while it identifies smaller immigrant core groups whose ancestry came from elsewhere.
claims.certainty_reason: This records what the study reports, read in the open copy linked under Sources.

open_questions.text: How far can a few dozen graves, mostly rich ones, stand for a whole people?
Genes, language and the name a group used for itself can travel separately. How do the studies connect them?
